faqs.question: Can I put widgets on my Mac desktop?
answer: Yes. macOS supports widgets on the desktop and in Notification Center. Apple says to Control-click the wallpaper, choose Edit Widgets, then click a widget or drag it to the position you want.

Arras uses independent borderless desktop windows rather than Apple’s fixed WidgetKit frames. Each photo can keep its own proportions, position, opacity, and layering instead of being confined to a system widget size.

sources.label: Apple Support: Add and customize widgets on Mac

faqs.question: How do I add a photo widget to my Mac desktop?
answer: For a built-in macOS widget, Control-click the wallpaper, choose Edit Widgets, find the Photos widget, and click or drag the size you want onto the desktop.

With Arras, install the app and add an exact photo from its menu bar icon, paste a copied image with Command-V, drag image files onto the menu bar icon, or import from Photos. Arras creates a separate desktop photo at the image’s true aspect ratio.

sources.label: Apple Support: Add and customize widgets on Mac

faqs.question: How to add a specific photo widget on a Mac?
answer: Apple notes that only widgets with an Edit option let you change what they show, so control over a specific image depends on the widget and macOS version.

Arras lets you choose the exact image directly: paste it, drag its file in, select it from Photos, capture part of the screen, or import a PDF page. The selected photo keeps its saved size and desktop position.

sources.label: Apple Support: Add and customize widgets on Mac

faqs.question: Can a Mac photo widget display images without cropping?
answer: Yes. Arras displays each desktop photo at its original aspect ratio, so a panorama remains wide and a portrait remains vertical without forced cropping, black bars, or a fixed square frame.

You can drag a corner to resize while the aspect ratio stays locked. For rotating photo sets, Dynamic sizing lets each image use its own true proportions, while Fixed sizing is available when you intentionally want a locked frame.

faqs.question: How to get rid of the photo widget on Mac desktop?
answer: For a standard macOS widget, Control-click it and choose Remove Widget, or open Edit Widgets mode and click its Remove button.
For an Arras photo, right-click the photo window and choose Remove. Removing one Arras image does not reset the positions, sizes, or settings of the other desktop photos.

sources.label: Apple Support: Add and customize widgets on Mac

faqs.question: How to customize photo widgets on Mac?
answer: For a standard macOS widget, Control-click it to use any available Edit option, choose another supported size, or remove it. Apple also provides desktop settings for widget visibility and color treatment.

Arras adds per-photo controls for opacity, layering, locked placement, shape masks, mats, shadows, borders, vignettes, tilt, and Gallery, Polaroid, Minimal, or Modern presets. Photos can also sit behind desktop icons or float above other windows.

sources.label: Apple Support: Add and customize widgets on Mac

faqs.question: Can Arras rotate several photos in one widget?
answer: Yes. Arras can rotate several images in one desktop photo Space, with on-click or timed changes.

Dynamic sizing preserves each image’s individual aspect ratio. Fixed sizing is available when you intentionally want every image to use the same frame. Configure these controls in Arras rather than the macOS widget gallery.

faqs.question: Why does macOS say it cannot verify Arras?
answer: The current Arras download is not notarized, so macOS may block the first launch. This warning does not by itself establish whether an app is safe; download only from the official release and open it only if you trust its source.

After trying to open it, follow Apple’s guidance in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway. The Arras installation section also explains the Homebrew option and what removing the quarantine flag does.

sources.label: Apple Support: Safely open apps on your Mac

faqs.question: Which Macs can run Arras?
answer: The current Arras release requires macOS 14 Sonoma or later and its downloadable build supports Apple Silicon Macs. The project documentation says an Intel build can be compiled from source.

faqs.question: Is Arras free and open source?
answer: Yes. Arras is free and open source under the MIT License, with no subscription or account required. Start with the official Arras website for the app overview, compatibility, and installation instructions; GitHub hosts the source code and downloadable release files.
